name: survey-overlay-lifecycle
description: Survey confidence overlay lifecycle: fresh survey rendering → tick past stale threshold → new survey refreshes overlay → blast terrain remesh preserves overlay. FAILS until GameRenderer wires getSurveyOverlay().show() in syncFromContext().

steps.description: Test-only bootstrap, not a player action: hiring already grants the Rookie starting qualification (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION in Employee.ts, same for the UI hire button and this console command), so this only raises the level for the scenario's needs. No role tag -- there is no UI control for this and none should exist; the player-facing way to raise a skill is `employee train` at a training building. Command mode keeps running it unchanged; interaction mode keeps it as an unmarked (legacy) command step. Finding #15 class: the original command used positional args (`employee assign_skill 1 geology 5`) — assignSkillCommand requires the named form and silently rejected it ('Usage: employee assign_skill <id> skill:<category> level:1-5', never thrown), so this call and the one below failed on every run in this file's history. Fixed to the correct syntax.
Test-only bootstrap — see the assign_skill step above for why this stays an unmarked (legacy) command step in interaction mode too, and for the Finding #15 class fix.
Survey 1/2, round 1. Two surveyors, so both round-1 surveys are worked in parallel (unlike Finding #16's single-employee case) — real run confirms both complete cleanly.

expect.note: both round-1 surveys queued, neither completed yet
both round-1 surveys queued, neither completed yet

#547: tickEmployees claims both round-1 surveys on the very first of these ticks (both surveyors idle, both qualified), but their records now stay in pendingActions -- only status/holderId flip -- instead of being spliced out at claim time. Both surveyors are still many ticks from arriving at (20,20), so pendingActionCount must stay at 2 (unclaimed 0, not the pre-#547 behaviour where a claim alone dropped this to 0).

steps.description: #553: drill_hole is now a queued, vehicle-gated action -- a driller physically drives a drill_rig to each hole -- so this file (which pre-#553 never needed a driller at all) now needs one. campaign start has no staffed:true equivalent, so this is a manual hire + purchase, same pattern as survey-then-blast.json. Employee #3 -- #1 and #2 are the two surveyors hired above.

Left unmarked: hiring already grants blasting at Rookie (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION), but no role starts with driving.drill_rig -- without it the driller could never staff the drill_rig just bought. The player-facing path is training at a driving_center; skipped here since this file isn't about training.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:4 depth:6 start:20,20
steps.description: The (20,20)-(24,24) rectangle (4x4) computes round(4/3)+1=2 per axis at the panel's default 3m spacing (never touched in this file) — the declared 2x2 by coincidence, no stepper click needed. #553: confirming the grid queues 4 drill_hole PendingActions and pushes 4 PlannedHoles into plannedDrillHoles — none drilled yet, so holeCount stays 0 right after confirm.

expect.note: 2 rows x 2 cols = 4 holes ordered (ghosts), none drilled yet (#553)

steps.description: #553: drain the ordered plan in bounded tick chunks -- each chunk is followed by `event choose 0` since a `tick` command stops dead the instant a timer event fires mid-block (events.ts). No staffed:true near-origin spawn here (campaign start), so this single driller/drill_rig takes longer than the usual 4-hole recipe. Sandbox-measured: all 4 holes land by cumulative +130 ticks post-drill_plan (50+50+30) -- trimmed from an earlier 5x50=250 padding that ran well-being (already at 6.2 before this block, with no Living Quarters anywhere in this file) to a sustained 0 long enough to trigger the #553-unrelated WORKER REVOLT game-over during the since-removed 4th chunk. `revolted` stays false through the trimmed sequence (command-mode traced).
Third and final chunk — all 4 holes have landed by cumulative +130 ticks post-drill_plan (command-mode traced).

#554-followup round 2 (issue #586 CI): round 1's fix (3 rounds of tick 15 = 45 ticks, sized from a 43-tick command-mode measurement) still stalled in real interaction-mode CI -- root-caused via local reproduction to a genuine cross-mode divergence, not a timing race: the sole driller here collapses (fatigue hits its floor, tickNeedGauges/tickCollapse) partway through charging in interaction mode's own real trajectory, with no living_quarters anywhere in this file to shorten the recovery (NEED_REST_NO_BUILDING_DURATION_MULTIPLIER doubles it), stalling chargedCount at 1/4 for the remainder of the original 45-tick budget -- command mode's identical tick-for-tick trace does not hit the same collapse within that window. #554-followup round 3: a first attempt at 6 rounds (90 ticks) let all 4 holes charge by round 4 (60 ticks) but then burned 2 more rounds of pure dead padding (nothing left to charge) that pushed this file's already-thin wellBeing margin (no living_quarters anywhere, single driller/drill_rig, same class this file's own drilling-wait note above already trimmed padding to avoid) into a genuine worker_revolt during the trailing rounds -- the resulting level-end overlay then blocked the sequence step below. Trimmed to 4 rounds of tick 15 (60 ticks): comfortable margin over the measured collapse-and-recover-and-finish point, without the extra dead ticks that risked crossing REVOLT_TICKS=120 for no reason.

expect.note: a fired blast clears the plan back to zero
